title: The Prayer Room Between Two Trains
script: Narrator: [warmly] On a journey to visit my aunt, I had to change trains at a large station. The timetable gave me fifty minutes between services.
Narrator: I wanted to pray during the stop, but I did not know the building. The signs showed platforms, shops, and toilets, but I saw no prayer-room sign.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Instead of walking around with my heavy bag, I asked a staff member at the information desk.
Narrator: She checked a station map and showed me a quiet multi-faith room on the upper floor. She also marked the lift because one staircase was closed.
Narrator: [honestly] I confirmed the departure platform before leaving the desk. That simple step reduced my worry about missing the train.
Narrator: The room was clean and quiet. I had already made wudu before traveling, but washing facilities were available nearby.
Narrator: [carefully] I kept my ticket and phone inside my closed bag and placed it where I could see it without disturbing anyone.
Narrator: After prayer, I still had twenty-five minutes. I returned directly to the platform and checked the electronic board.
Narrator: [curious] The platform had changed from six to eight. Because I arrived early, I could move without running.
Narrator: Another passenger looked confused by the change, so I showed him the board and pointed toward the correct bridge.
Narrator: [relieved] The stop taught me that planning worship during travel includes practical questions. We can check times, facilities, luggage, and route changes.
Narrator: Asking staff is often faster and safer than trusting an old online comment about a station.
Narrator: [reflective] I now save a station map before longer journeys and allow extra time when I can.
Narrator: The prayer room gave me a calm center in a busy trip, and careful planning helped me leave it without panic.
